Canonicalize a statistic map to a Z-equivalent volume

Source: R/canonicalize.R
canonicalize.Rd

Convenience wrapper around canonicalize_stat() that returns only the Z-equivalent statistic map. This is the canonical first step before calling inference functions in neurothresh.

Usage

canonicalize(
  stat_vol,
  stat_type = c("Z", "t", "neglog10p"),
  df = NULL,
  tail = c("pos", "neg", "two"),
  p_side = c("one", "two"),
  sign_vol = NULL
)

Arguments

stat_vol

A NeuroVol object containing the statistical map

stat_type

Character string specifying the input type:

"Z"

Z-scores (identity transform)

"t"

t-statistics (requires df)

"neglog10p"

Negative log10 p-values

df

Degrees of freedom, required when stat_type = "t"

tail

Character string specifying the tail:

"pos"

Positive tail (activations)

"neg"

Negative tail (deactivations)

"two"

Two-sided test

p_side

Character string for -log10(p) inputs specifying whether the p-values are one-sided or two-sided: "one" or "two"

sign_vol

Optional NeuroVol providing sign information for -log10(p) inputs to recover directionality

Value

The Z-equivalent statistic volume (same type as stat_vol). For richer output (one-sided/two-sided p-values, mask), call canonicalize_stat() directly.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
zvol <- canonicalize(t_map, stat_type = "t", df = 24)
res <- hier_scan(zvol, parcels = atlas, alpha = 0.05)
} # }
